text.p: Pharmaceutical group F.H Faulding and Co Ltd on Thursday welcomed the Australian government's new policies for the industry, saying it had delivered a positive resolution to some very complex issues.
The government said on Tuesday it would invest A$300 million over five years in a new programme to follow the existing Factor (f) scheme, due to end in July 1999.

The scheme compensates drug companies for lower than average drug prices in Australia with payments for investment in research and development and meeting targets on export and value-added manufacturing.

Faulding chief executive Ed Tweddell said despite a reduction in the level of funding, the replacement of the Factor (f) scheme and certainty to 2004 demonstrated government commitment to the continued growth of the industry.
Faulding looked forward to working with the government on the development of guidelines and details on implementation to ensure it provided for the most effective allocation of funds, he said.

Tweddell also welcomed proposed changes to patents law to provide for extensions of up to five years for 20-year standard pharmaceutical patents which would also allow springboarding (preparation for generic copying) for eligible patents.
Faulding was particularly pleased to see the balance struck by the government on the issue which would maintain Australia's competitiveness as a site for generic development and export, he said.
